title: AI Labelling Is Now Law
intro: The EU AI Act's transparency rules have been in force since 2 August 2026. A sparkle icon is not a label.

learn.title: What must be disclosed
learn.text:
Any product whose AI output reaches people in the EU must disclose:

• **Chatbots and AI agents** — users must know they're not talking to a person
• **Realistic images, audio or video** of real things (deepfakes)
• **Unreviewed AI text on matters of public interest**
• **Emotion recognition and biometric categorisation**

Public interest covers health, safety, environment, economy, finance, politics, science and culture — product claims touching these count.

options: Unreviewed AI text about a health claim
try.explain: Most AI-assisted work is exempt; it's the generated and unreviewed output that isn't.

right.label: Usually exempt
items: Human-reviewed text with a named editor

learn.title: What counts as review
learn.text:
**A skim before publishing isn't review.** Editing must be substantive, and someone named takes responsibility.

Summaries, composite images, substantive rewrites, and adding or removing elements in photographs all count as generation rather than assistance.

try.q: Your team runs AI-drafted copy past an editor who scans it quickly. Is it exempt?
options: Only if the editor is named
try.explain: A skim isn't review; someone named must take responsibility.

learn.title: How to label
learn.text:
Use the **EU mark plus plain text**. The label must be **visible, persistent and accessible** — not a decorative sparkle, not a tooltip, not something that disappears on scroll.

It also has to survive the places the content travels to: a label that only exists in your interface doesn't help when the image is shared.

try.q: What is wrong with a sparkle icon as an AI label?
options: It isn't recognised outside the EU
try.explain: Icon plus plain text, visible and persistent. It carries no meaning.

test.q: Since when have the transparency rules applied?
test.explain: In force for anything EU users see.

test.q: Who do the rules apply to?
options: Any product whose AI output reaches EU users
Products with more than 10,000 EU users

test.q: Which topics count as public interest?
options: Health, safety, environment, economy, finance, politics, science, culture

test.q: What must a label be, besides visible?
test.explain: It can't vanish on scroll or hide behind a tooltip.

test.q: Does adding or removing elements in a photo count as generation?
options: Only if the result is realistic
test.explain: Along with summaries, composites and substantive rewrites.
